text:
maria: FYI CS is reporting a spike of 502/504s and request timeouts hitting hosted inference routes starting ~23:40 UTC. Customers include two large tenants. Opening thread to coordinate mitigation and repro.

support-bot: alert: hosted-inference-gateway:502_rate_increase detected at 2026-03-17T23:42:10Z (p95 latency spike).

sam: jumping in. any obvious deploys or autoscaler events around 23:30-23:45?

nate: checking deploys now. no recent prod rollouts in that window. autoscaler shows several node terminations in ap-northeast-1 between 23:35-23:41.

lee: looking at auth proxy logs for that window — I see elevated 504s from upstream auth service for a subset of tokens. Correlation: requests that go through the new auth proxy path are timing out.

maria: CS thread shows client errors also include repeated 429s then 5xx. Could be retry amplification.

sam: can someone dump a sample stack of failing request headers/route? paste small snippet (redact tokens).

lee: posted snippet: ```
PROXY_ROUTE: /v1/generate
X-Client-ID: acct-42
Auth-Path: /auth/validate
Upstream: auth-01.apn1.internal
Status: 504
Latency: auth=2.1s gateway=3.6s
```

nate: I see KV-cache miss storms from those tenants at same time — cache warmup triggered large fanout to model shards. Combined with auth slow path and node terminations, request queueing blew timeouts.

maria: mitigation plan ideas: 1) enable fast-fail fallback to lighter auth-check (grace) for affected customers; 2) temporarily increase request timeout and queue depth for hosted-inference gateway; 3) scale up dedicated pool in ap-northeast-1. preferences?

sam: I'd prefer 2) + 3) first (less risky). 1) has auth/security implications; need approvals from security/CS.

lee: rolling a config change to increase gateway request timeout from 8s -> 12s for route /v1/generate on ap-northeast-1. Applying now canary to 10% of traffic.

support-bot: deploybot: config-change applied to gateway-canary (10%). Monitoring p95 for canary.

maria: nate, can you trigger a quick scale up of pool ( +50% ) in ap-northeast-1 reserved pool? autoscaler seems overwhelmed.

nate: scaling up reserved pool now, ETA ~3m. Kicking off node spin up and warmup.

cs-team: customer impacted requesting ETA for fix — two paying customers seeing increased errors. We need a clear comms line.

maria: CS: send interim note: "We're aware of increased timeouts and have applied temporary gateway timeout increase and are scaling capacity in region. We expect improvements within 10 minutes."

cs-team: sending now, adding that we're prioritizing their traffic. :thumbsup:

lee: canary p95 reduced slightly after timeout change but still seeing auth upstream tail at 2s for some requests. Might need short-circuit for repetitive token checks (cache validation).

nate: scaled nodes are booting; warmup logs show kv-cache warmups in progress. Eviction rate dropping.

sam: observe for 10m, if errors continue we consider routing affected customers to fallback region (eu-west) and enabling auth-grace with security approval.

maria: agree. also action items for postmortem: - refine kv-cache warmup to avoid thundering herd - add autoscaler throttling tolerance to avoid terminations during spikes - create an auth proxy fallback mode with audit trail and CS playbook for opt-in - improve alerting to correlate auth upstream latency and kv-cache misses

lee: logging note: add sampling of auth response bodies for 5xx/504s (PII-safe) so we can triage root cause next day.

support-bot: metric update: errors in ap-northeast-1 dropped 70% at 23:52 after scale/warmup. continued monitoring.

maria: great. continue watch. Nate/Lee/Sam, please own next 1h on-call rotation for followups. CS to hold customers for updates. I'll open a postmortem doc and link back here.

nate: on it. tagging followups in tracker: INC-2026-147.

cs-team: thanks — customers acknowledged note and will monitor.

sam: quick repro steps recorded for postmortem: 1) send burst of 10k auth-validated requests with varied token TTLs to /v1/generate in ap-northeast-1 2) observe kv-cache miss rate and auth upstream latency 3) reproduce autoscaler churn by simulating node failure signals. share scripts in doc.

maria: perfect. I'll draft action items and owners. We'll run a dedicated dry-run of the warmup mitigation next week.

support-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. incident_owner: maria.

lee: hooking a follow-up meeting invite for 2026-03-18 09:00 UTC to review postmortem draft.

maria: thanks all. closing thread for active coordination, leave for async PMs and postmortem edits.
